_env_file_quoting: In /etc/relayd/relayd.env, single-quote every value: KEY='value'. systemd's EnvironmentFile parser and a shell's `.` both strip exactly one layer of matching single quotes, so single-quoting is the only form that survives both. Unquoted or double-quoted values (notably the CODEX_WORKSPACES JSON) lose their inner quotes when the file is sourced.
_comment: relayd example configuration. relayd is configured through environment variables (see /etc/relayd/relayd.env on a systemd install); this file documents the supported knobs and their defaults. Values here are PLACEHOLDERS — never commit real hostnames, subjects, or keys.

server.RELAYD_LISTEN_MODE_comment: direct = plain HTTP listener behind a TLS-terminating gateway that forwards X-SSL-Client-Verify / X-SSL-Client-S-DN; tunneled = the same router served through the broker with TLS terminated on this node (the forwarded-subject headers are then derived from the peer certificate and any client-supplied ones are dropped); both = run the two side by side.
server.RELAYD_ALLOWED_CERT_SUBJECTS_comment: Allowed client-certificate subject DNs. PREFERRED FORM: a JSON array of complete DNs. An RFC 2253 DN contains commas (CN=device,OU=Devices,O=Relay), so the legacy comma-separated form below can only express single-RDN subjects — a multi-RDN DN written that way is shredded into fragments and the device 403s forever. A newline-separated value is also accepted. RELAYD_ALLOWED_CERT_SUBJECTS wins when non-empty.
server.CODEX_ALLOWED_CERT_SUBJECTS_comment: Legacy name and legacy comma-separated format, still honored when RELAYD_ALLOWED_CERT_SUBJECTS is empty. SINGLE-RDN SUBJECTS ONLY — use the JSON form above for anything realistic.

pairing._comment: Onboarding. `relayd pair` persists a single-use 15-minute session into the store and exits; the DAEMON serves POST /v1/pair on its own listener and redeems it. That listener is never the mTLS data listener — relayd refuses to start if the two ports collide.
pairing.RELAYD_PAIRING_HOST_comment: Defaults to 127.0.0.1, INDEPENDENTLY of CODEX_API_HOST. This listener is plain HTTP, needs no client certificate and mints device certificates, and the gateway that terminates TLS for the data port is not in front of it — so moving it off loopback is an explicit opt-in you make here, never a side effect of exposing the data listener.
pairing.RELAYD_PAIRING_PORT_comment: Unset (or 0) = the kernel assigns a free port at bind time, which the daemon logs and records in <CODEX_DATA_DIR>/pairing/listener.json so `relayd pair` prints the right URL. relayd never claims a port you did not give it (it used to default to CODEX_API_PORT + 1 and kill a co-located daemon with EADDRINUSE). Set it — as dist/install.sh does — when the address must be stable for a gateway or an SSH tunnel. Must differ from CODEX_API_PORT.
pairing.RELAYD_PAIRING_ADVERTISE_comment: Optional public base URL that `relayd pair` prints as the address the phone should reach; unset means derive it from the bind address.
pairing.RELAYD_PAIRING_AUTOALLOW_comment: Add the subject of the certificate this node just minted in a successful pairing to the client-cert allowlist, appended to <CODEX_DATA_DIR>/allowed-cert-subjects.json (0600) and audited as cert_subject_allowlisted. With this false a freshly paired device receives a valid certificate and is then 403'd until an operator edits the allowlist and restarts.

tunnel._comment: Tunneled listen mode. Only read when RELAYD_LISTEN_MODE is tunneled or both; the broker endpoint is assigned at enrollment. Placeholders only.
tunnel.RELAYD_TUNNEL_SUFFIX_comment: The node dials out and is reached at <node-id><suffix>; that name is the SNI the broker routes on and the SAN the node TLS server certificate is issued for (created automatically from the node CA).
tunnel.RELAYD_TUNNEL_SNI_comment: Optional explicit override; leave unset to use <node-id> + RELAYD_TUNNEL_SUFFIX.
tunnel.RELAYD_TUNNEL_BACKOFF_comment: Reconnect backoff: base doubles per attempt, jittered to 50-100% of the delay, capped at max, reset on a successful registration.
